formats.key: deposit(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 maxAmount0, uint128 maxAmount1, uint128 minLiquidity)
effects: Pulls up to maxAmount0 of token0 and up to maxAmount1 of token1 from the signer (transferFrom to the Core accountant) into position id.
In a native-token pool (token0 = address(0)) pays token0 as ETH out of msg.value; ETH not used stays in the Positions contract and anyone can take it with refundNativeToken.
Adds at least minLiquidity liquidity to the position of NFT id between tickLower and tickUpper, in the pool given by token0, token1 and config (fee, extension).
formats.shown: "Add liquidity" with position ID, maximum token 0 and token 1 amounts, raw minimum liquidity, raw ticks and an optional raw pool config; no native value.

findings.title: deposit is payable and spends msg.value in native pools, but no @.value field is shown.
findings.evidence: BasePositions.handleLockData: `SafeTransferLib.safeTransferETH(address(ACCOUNTANT), amount0);` for token0 == NATIVE_TOKEN_ADDRESS; deposit is `public payable`. Descriptor fields: no `@.value`.

findings.title: deposit maxAmount0 uses tokenPath poolKey.token0 without nativeCurrencyAddress, so native ETH pools render badly.
findings.evidence: constants.sol: `address constant NATIVE_TOKEN_ADDRESS = address(0);` Descriptor: maxAmount0 `"tokenPath": "poolKey.token0"` with no nativeCurrencyAddress.

findings.title: deposit shows the pool config as one raw bytes32; the pool extension and fee are unreadable.
findings.evidence: poolConfig.sol: `extension(config) = shr(96, config)`, `fee = and(shr(32, config), 0xffffffffffffffff)`. Descriptor: poolKey.config format raw, visible optional.
findings.fix: Show poolKey.config.[0:20] as addressName 'Pool extension' and keep the raw config optional.

findings.title: deposit interpolatedIntent 'Add liquidity' omits the tokens, the maximum amounts and the position.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "interpolatedIntent": "Add liquidity".
findings.fix: Use "Add up to {maxAmount0} and {maxAmount1} to position {id}".

findings.title: deposit minimum liquidity and ticks have no unit or price format; they stay raw.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: minLiquidity, tickLower, tickUpper format raw; handleLockData: `if (liquidity < minLiquidity) revert DepositFailedDueToSlippage`.

formats.key: mintAndDeposit((address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 maxAmount0, uint128 maxAmount1, uint128 minLiquidity)
effects: Mints a new position NFT to the signer with a pseudo-random salt.
Pulls up to maxAmount0 of token0 and up to maxAmount1 of token1 from the signer into the new position.
In a native-token pool pays token0 as ETH from msg.value; unused ETH stays in the contract, takeable by anyone via refundNativeToken.
Adds at least minLiquidity liquidity between tickLower and tickUpper in the pool given by token0, token1 and config.
formats.shown: "Create liquidity position" / "Add liquidity" with maximum token 0 and token 1 amounts, raw minimum liquidity, raw ticks and optional raw pool config; no native value.

findings.title: mintAndDeposit is payable and spends msg.value in native pools, but no @.value field is shown.
findings.evidence: BasePositions.mintAndDeposit `external payable` calls deposit; handleLockData sends `safeTransferETH(address(ACCOUNTANT), amount0)` for native token0. No `@.value` field.

findings.title: mintAndDeposit maxAmount0 has no nativeCurrencyAddress for native ETH pools with token0 = address(0).
findings.evidence: constants.sol `NATIVE_TOKEN_ADDRESS = address(0)`; descriptor maxAmount0 params only `tokenPath: poolKey.token0`.

findings.title: mintAndDeposit shows pool config raw; extension address and fee tier are not readable.
findings.evidence: Case 0 screen: 'Pool config' = 0x000…000; poolConfig.sol `extension = shr(96, config)`.

findings.title: mintAndDeposit interpolatedIntent 'Add liquidity' differs from intent and omits amounts and the new NFT.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: intent "Create liquidity position", interpolatedIntent "Add liquidity".
findings.fix: Use "Create position with up to {maxAmount0} and {maxAmount1}".

findings.title: mintAndDeposit test covers only an ERC20 pool with zero value, not the native ETH path.
findings.evidence: Case 0: value "0", token0 USDC, token1 WETH; native branch in handleLockData untested.
findings.fix: Add a case with token0 = address(0) and a non-zero value.

formats.key: mintAndDepositWithSalt(bytes32 salt, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 maxAmount0, uint128 maxAmount1, uint128 minLiquidity)
effects: Mints a position NFT to the signer with an id derived from the signer and salt.
Pulls up to maxAmount0 of token0 and up to maxAmount1 of token1 from the signer into the position.
In a native-token pool pays token0 as ETH from msg.value; unused ETH stays in the contract, takeable by anyone via refundNativeToken.

formats.key: collectFees(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper)
effects: Collects all accrued swap fees of position id and sends them in token0 and token1 to the signer.
The protocol keeps about 10% of the collected fees (SWAP_PROTOCOL_FEE_X64 = 0x1999999999999999).
Any ETH sent with the call stays in the contract and anyone can take it with refundNativeToken.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 liquidity)
effects: Removes liquidity from position id and sends token0 and token1 to the signer, with no minimum amount.
Always also collects all accrued fees of the position to the signer (withFees = true), minus ~10% protocol fee.
Any ETH sent with the call stays in the contract and anyone can take it.
formats.shown: "Withdraw position {id}" with position ID, raw liquidity, pool tokens, raw ticks, optional config; no native value.

findings.title: withdraw is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent with it.
findings.evidence: BasePositions.withdraw(id,poolKey,tickLower,tickUpper,liquidity) `public payable`; no `@.value` field.

findings.title: withdraw always collects fees too, but intent and fields do not say so.
findings.evidence: BasePositions.withdraw: `withdraw(id, poolKey, tickLower, tickUpper, liquidity, address(msg.sender), true)`. Intent "Withdraw liquidity".
findings.fix: Change intent to "Withdraw liquidity and fees".

findings.title: withdraw has no minimum-out; token amounts depend on pool price and liquidity is raw.
findings.evidence: handleLockData: `withdrawnAmount0 = uint128(-balanceUpdate.delta0())`; no min parameter in the ABI.

findings.quote: BasePositions.sol `function collectFees(uint256 id, PoolKey memory poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper) public payable authorizedForNft(id)`; PayableMulticallable.refundNativeToken `safeTransferETH(msg.sender, address(this).balance)`; no `@.value` field

findings.format: refundNativeToken()
findings.title: refundNativeToken is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)
findings.reason: The contract's balance already includes msg.value, so this call always sends the attached ETH, plus any leftover, back to the caller in the same call. The signer cannot lose what they attach. The screen also shows the caller as the recipient (`@.from`).
findings.quote: PayableMulticallable.sol refundNativeToken: `if (address(this).balance != 0) { SafeTransferLib.safeTransferETH(msg.sender, address(this).balance); }`

findings.format: deposit(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 maxAmount0, uint128 maxAmount1, uint128 minLiquidity)
findings.title: deposit is payable and spends msg.value in native pools, but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The displayed token maxima bound liquidity payments, but do not bound attached ETH. Deposit forwards native payment and retains any excess without an automatic refund.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, deposit: `public payable authorizedForNft(id)`; handleLockData: `if (amount0 > maxAmount0 || amount1 > maxAmount1) revert DepositFailedDueToPriceMovement();` and `SafeTransferLib.safeTransferETH(address(ACCOUNTANT), amount0);`. descriptor.json, deposit: `"label": "Maximum token 0"`, `"label": "Maximum token 1"`; no `@.value` field.

findings.format: mintAndDeposit((address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 maxAmount0, uint128 maxAmount1, uint128 minLiquidity)
findings.title: mintAndDeposit is payable and spends msg.value in native pools, but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The function calls deposit internally, which accepts attached ETH and retains any excess over the native payment. The displayed maxima do not disclose or limit that excess.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, mintAndDeposit: `external payable` and `(liquidity, amount0, amount1) = deposit(id, poolKey, tickLower, tickUpper, maxAmount0, maxAmount1, minLiquidity);`; handleLockData: `SafeTransferLib.safeTransferETH(address(ACCOUNTANT), amount0);`. descriptor.json, mintAndDeposit: `"intent": "Create liquidity position"`, fields include `maxAmount0` and `maxAmount1`, but no `@.value`.

findings.format: mintAndDepositWithSalt(bytes32 salt, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 maxAmount0, uint128 maxAmount1, uint128 minLiquidity)
findings.title: mintAndDepositWithSalt is payable and spends msg.value in native pools, but no @.value is shown.
findings.reason: The salted wrapper calls deposit internally without restricting or refunding attached ETH. Displayed token maxima do not cover excess ETH retained by the contract.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, mintAndDepositWithSalt: `external payable`, `id = mint(salt);` and `(liquidity, amount0, amount1) = deposit(id, poolKey, tickLower, tickUpper, maxAmount0, maxAmount1, minLiquidity);`. descriptor.json, mintAndDepositWithSalt: `"intent": "Create salted liquidity"`; fields show `salt`, token maxima, liquidity and pool configuration, but no `@.value`.

findings.format: collectFees(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper)
findings.title: collectFees is payable, ignores msg.value, and no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: A successful fee collection retains attached ETH separately from the fees paid by the accountant. Refund requires a separate call and is available to any caller.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, collectFees without recipient: `(amount0, amount1) = collectFees(id, poolKey, tickLower, tickUpper, msg.sender);`; handleLockData: `ACCOUNTANT.withdrawTwo(poolKey.token0, poolKey.token1, recipient, amount0, amount1);`. PayableMulticallable.sol, refundNativeToken: `SafeTransferLib.safeTransferETH(msg.sender, address(this).balance);`. descriptor.json, collectFees: `"intent": "Collect position fees"`; no `@.value` field.

findings.format: collectFees(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, address recipient)
findings.title: collectFees with recipient is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: The payable function collects fees through withdraw without using or refunding attached ETH. The recipient field describes fee proceeds, not the additional ETH retained.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, collectFees with recipient: `public payable authorizedForNft(id)` and `(amount0, amount1) = withdraw(id, poolKey, tickLower, tickUpper, 0, recipient, true);`. descriptor.json, this overload: `"intent": "Collect position fees"`, `"path": "recipient"`; no `@.value` field.

findings.format: withdraw(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 liquidity)
findings.title: withdraw is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent with it.
findings.reason: The withdrawal leaves attached ETH in the Positions contract while the accountant pays withdrawal proceeds. No displayed field states that additional outgoing ETH.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, withdraw without recipient: `public payable` and `(amount0, amount1) = withdraw(id, poolKey, tickLower, tickUpper, liquidity, address(msg.sender), true);`; handleLockData: `ACCOUNTANT.withdrawTwo(poolKey.token0, poolKey.token1, recipient, amount0, amount1);`. descriptor.json, this overload: `"intent": "Withdraw liquidity"`, `"path": "liquidity"`; no `@.value`.

findings.format: withdraw(uint256 id, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tickLower, int32 tickUpper, uint128 liquidity, address recipient, bool withFees)
findings.title: withdraw with recipient is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: The payable withdrawal does not reject or refund attached ETH. Its liquidity and recipient fields do not disclose ETH retained independently of withdrawal proceeds.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, withdraw with recipient: `public payable authorizedForNft(id)` and `lock(abi.encode(CALL_TYPE_WITHDRAW, id, poolKey, tickLower, tickUpper, liquidity, recipient, withFees))`. BaseLocker.sol, lock: `call(gas(), target, 0, result, add(len, 4), 0, 0)`. descriptor.json, this overload: `"intent": "Withdraw liquidity"`; no `@.value`.

findings.format: maybeInitializePool((address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tick)
findings.title: maybeInitializePool is payable, ignores msg.value, and no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: For an initialized pool, the payable function returns after reading pool state and retains all attached ETH. Neither the intent nor the fields disclose that transfer.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, maybeInitializePool: `external payable`; `sqrtRatio = CORE.poolState(poolKey.toPoolId()).sqrtRatio(); if (sqrtRatio.isZero()) { initialized = true; sqrtRatio = CORE.initializePool(poolKey, tick); }`. descriptor.json: `"intent": "Initialize pool if needed"`; fields are pool tokens, tick and config, without `@.value`.

findings.format: burn(uint256 id)
findings.title: burn is payable, ignores msg.value, and no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: An authorized burn retains attached ETH; its NFT authorization does not check transaction value. The screen only describes burning the NFT.
findings.quote: BaseNonfungibleToken.sol, burn: `function burn(uint256 id) external payable authorizedForNft(id) { _burn(id); }` and `No fees are collected; any msg.value sent is ignored.` descriptor.json, burn: `"intent": "Burn position NFT"`, sole field `"path": "id"`.

findings.format: multicall(bytes[] data)
findings.title: multicall is payable and funds native deposits, but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The override bypasses the base multicall zero-value check and does not automatically refund ETH. Even an empty batch retains attached ETH, which the action field does not show.
findings.quote: PayableMulticallable.sol, multicall: `function multicall(bytes[] calldata data) public payable override returns (bytes[] memory) { _multicallDirectReturn(_multicall(data)); }`. Multicallable.sol, _multicall: `if (data.length) {`. descriptor.json, multicall: `"intent": "Batch position actions"`, sole field `"path": "data.[]"`, with no amountPath or `@.value`.

findings.format: approve(address account, uint256 id)
findings.title: approve is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: A successful approval retains attached ETH without a value check or refund. The screen shows the approval account and NFT only.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, approve: `function approve(address account, uint256 id) public payable virtual { _approve(msg.sender, account, id); }`. descriptor.json, approve: `"intent": "Approve position NFT"`; fields `account` and `id`, without `@.value`.

findings.format: transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id)
findings.title: transferFrom is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: A valid NFT transfer accepts and retains ETH independently of the NFT transfer. The displayed sender, recipient and ID do not state that ETH payment.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, transferFrom: `function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id) public payable virtual` and `sstore(ownershipSlot, xor(ownershipPacked, xor(from, to)))`. descriptor.json, transferFrom: `"intent": "Transfer position NFT"`; fields `from`, `to`, `id`, without `@.value`.

findings.format: safeTransferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id)
findings.title: safeTransferFrom is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: A successful transfer to an EOA retains attached ETH without making a receiver callback. No screen field shows that retained ETH.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256): `public payable virtual { transferFrom(from, to, id); if (_hasCode(to)) _checkOnERC721Received(from, to, id, ""); }`. descriptor.json, this overload: `"intent": "Transfer position NFT"`; fields `from`, `to`, `id`, without `@.value`.

findings.format: safeTransferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id, bytes data)
findings.title: safeTransferFrom with data is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: This overload also retains attached ETH on a successful transfer to an EOA. Showing transfer data does not disclose transaction value.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, safeTransferFrom with data: `public payable virtual` and `transferFrom(from, to, id); if (_hasCode(to)) _checkOnERC721Received(from, to, id, data);`. descriptor.json, this overload: `"intent": "Transfer position NFT"`; fields `from`, `to`, `id`, `data`, without `@.value`.

findings.format: mint()
findings.title: mint() is payable, ignores msg.value, and no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: Ignoring msg.value leaves ETH in the contract; it does not return ETH to the signer. The mint screen contains no fields.
findings.quote: BaseNonfungibleToken.sol, mint(): `function mint() public payable returns (uint256 id)` and `id = mint(salt);`; devdoc: `No fees are collected; any msg.value sent is ignored.` descriptor.json, mint(): `"intent": "Mint position NFT", "fields": []`.

findings.format: mint(bytes32 salt)
findings.title: mint(salt) is payable, ignores msg.value, and no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: A successful salted mint retains attached ETH with no value check or refund. The salt field does not disclose that transfer.
findings.quote: BaseNonfungibleToken.sol, mint(bytes32): `function mint(bytes32 salt) public payable returns (uint256 id) { id = saltToId(msg.sender, salt); _mint(msg.sender, id); }`. descriptor.json, mint(bytes32): `"intent": "Mint salted position NFT"`, sole field `"path": "salt"`.

findings.format: transferOwnership(address newOwner)
findings.title: transferOwnership is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: A valid owner can transfer ownership with nonzero ETH, which remains in the contract. The owner and zero-address checks do not restrict transaction value.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/auth/Ownable.sol, transferOwnership: `function transferOwnership(address newOwner) public payable virtual onlyOwner` and `_setOwner(newOwner);`. descriptor.json, transferOwnership: `"intent": "Transfer contract ownership"`, sole field `"path": "newOwner"`.

findings.format: renounceOwnership()
findings.title: renounceOwnership is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: Successful renunciation by the owner retains attached ETH. The screen describes renunciation but contains no amount field.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/auth/Ownable.sol, renounceOwnership: `function renounceOwnership() public payable virtual onlyOwner { _setOwner(address(0)); }`. descriptor.json, renounceOwnership: `"intent": "Renounce ownership", "fields": []`.

findings.format: requestOwnershipHandover()
findings.title: requestOwnershipHandover is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: The request records an expiry without rejecting or returning attached ETH. The screen has no fields disclosing the transfer.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/auth/Ownable.sol, requestOwnershipHandover: `function requestOwnershipHandover() public payable virtual` and `sstore(keccak256(0x0c, 0x20), expires)`. descriptor.json, requestOwnershipHandover: `"intent": "Request ownership handover", "fields": []`.

findings.format: cancelOwnershipHandover()
findings.title: cancelOwnershipHandover is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: Cancellation clears the request and retains attached ETH without a value check. The screen contains no amount field.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/auth/Ownable.sol, cancelOwnershipHandover: `function cancelOwnershipHandover() public payable virtual` and `sstore(keccak256(0x0c, 0x20), 0)`. descriptor.json, cancelOwnershipHandover: `"intent": "Cancel ownership handover", "fields": []`.

findings.format: completeOwnershipHandover(address pendingOwner)
findings.title: completeOwnershipHandover is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: Completing a valid handover retains attached ETH. The authorization and request-expiry checks do not prevent nonzero value.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/auth/Ownable.sol, completeOwnershipHandover: `function completeOwnershipHandover(address pendingOwner) public payable virtual onlyOwner` and `_setOwner(pendingOwner);`. descriptor.json, completeOwnershipHandover: `"intent": "Complete ownership handover"`, sole field `"path": "pendingOwner"`.

findings.format: withdrawProtocolFees(address token0, address token1, uint128 amount0, uint128 amount1, address recipient)
findings.title: withdrawProtocolFees is payable, but no @.value field shows ETH sent.
findings.reason: The accountant pays protocol fees while attached ETH remains in Positions. The displayed withdrawal amounts do not describe or bound that separate incoming ETH.
findings.quote: BasePositions.sol, withdrawProtocolFees: `external payable onlyOwner` and `lock(abi.encode(CALL_TYPE_WITHDRAW_PROTOCOL_FEES, token0, token1, amount0, amount1, recipient));`; handleLockData: `ACCOUNTANT.withdrawTwo(token0, token1, recipient, amount0, amount1);`. descriptor.json: `"intent": "Withdraw protocol fees"`; fields `token0`, `amount0`, `token1`, `amount1`, `recipient`, without `@.value`.

findings.format: refundNativeToken()
findings.title: refundNativeToken is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)
findings.reason: A successful call returns the entire balance, including attached ETH, to the caller. This matches the stated refund and the guide's exception for funds returning to the caller.
findings.quote: PayableMulticallable.sol, refundNativeToken: `if (address(this).balance != 0) { SafeTransferLib.safeTransferETH(msg.sender, address(this).balance); }`. descriptor.json: `"intent": "Refund unused native token"`, `"path": "@.from", "label": "Recipient"`. Registry .github/scripts/ai-review/prompt.md, not_critical item 4: `funds that return to the caller. Not a different recipient; not a finding`.
